In 2021, worldwide box office revenue grew by over 80 percent and reached 21.3 billion dollars. 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' starring Tom Holland in the lead, continued its record-breaking spree at the box office. The film hit another major milestone at the worldwide box office, surpassing James Cameron's 'Avatar: The Way of Water' to become the third highest-grossing film of all time.

# Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' overtakes James Cameron's 'Avatar: The Way Of Water' with USD 2.33 billion haul; becomes third highest-grossing film of all time
## 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' hits USD 2.33 billion
For the fifth weekend in a row, 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' topped the North American box office. It grossed USD 22.2 million in U.S. and Canadian theatres, according to studio estimates Sunday, bringing its worldwide total to USD 2.33 billion and making it the third highest-grossing film of all time.

# Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' overtakes James Cameron's 'Avatar: The Way Of Water' with USD 2.33 billion haul; becomes third highest-grossing film of all time
## 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' beats 'Avatar: The Way of Water'
The Tom Holland-led superhero blockbuster with its earnings crossing the USD 2.33 billion mark, has now edged past 'Avatar: The Way of Water', which finished its theatrical run with approximately USD 2.32 billion. The film's latest earnings represent a drop of just 44% from week 4.

# Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' overtakes James Cameron's 'Avatar: The Way Of Water' with USD 2.33 billion haul; becomes third highest-grossing film of all time
## Top five highest-grossing films worldwide
'Avatar' - USD 2.92 billion'Avengers: Endgame' - USD 2.79 billion'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' - USD 2.33 billion'Avatar: The Way of Water' - USD 2.32 billion'Titanic' - USD 2.25 billion

# Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' overtakes James Cameron's 'Avatar: The Way Of Water' with USD 2.33 billion haul; becomes third highest-grossing film of all time
## 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' domestic box office collections
The film has also amassed a staggering USD 891 million at the domestic box office, putting it within striking distance of another box office record.'Brand New Day' reportedly needs to cross USD 936 million domestically to overtake 'Star Wars: The Force Awakens', which currently holds the record for the highest-grossing movie of all time in North America. If it clears that mark, the 'Spider-Man' blockbuster would then have its sights on becoming the first film ever to gross USD 1 billion at the North American box office.

# Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' overtakes James Cameron's 'Avatar: The Way Of Water' with USD 2.33 billion haul; becomes third highest-grossing film of all time
## Tom Holland becomes third highest grossing actor
Tom Holland has also officially become the third highest-grossing actor of all time, behind Zoe Saldana and Scarlett Johansson. At just 30, Holland is also the youngest actor to feature on the list, with his impressive box office haul driven largely by his hugely successful run as 'Spider-Man'. With 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' continuing its record-breaking theatrical run.

## 'Coyote vs. Acme' off to a flying start
Three years after Warner Bros. abruptly canned 'Coyote vs. Acme,' the Looney Tunes feature film that was given a new lease on life by Ketchup Entertainment debuted with an estimated USD 15.5 million in ticket sales over the weekend.'Coyote vs. Acme', which had been relegated to the dust heap, fared best of the newcomers, debuting in second place. The film, however, scored a decent, hard-earned opening. In 2023, Warner Bros. canceled any release of the completed film, preferring to take a tax write off on a movie originally produced for its streaming service, HBO Max. Warner also shelved 'Batgirl' and 'Scoob! Holiday Haunt', both of which remain unreleased.'Coyote vs. Acme', based on an Ian Frazier 'Shouts and Murmurs' New Yorker column, is about Wile E. Coyote suing the Acme Corporation for its faulty products. It stars Will Forte, John Cena, Lana Condor and Eric Bauza. The film, a hybrid of live-action and animation directed by Dave Green, cost USD 70 million to make. But despite good test screening scores, Warner Bros. opted to ax the completed film. After an outcry, the studio put the film up for sale. Early last year, Ketchup Entertainment acquired worldwide distribution rights for about USD 50 million.Reviews and audience scores were also good. Moviegoers gave it an "A" CinemaScore. Critics were just as enthusiastic. On Rotten Tomatoes, it rated 95% fresh.While the result might have counted as a disappointment for some USD 70 million movies, the opening weekend for 'Coyote vs. Acme' was the best ever for Ketchup. The indie distributor's previous high was 2024's 'The Day the Earth Blew Up' (a $3.1 million opening), another Warner-made Looney Tunes castoff.

## 'The Dog Stars' makes USD 8 million debut
The Ridley Scott action drama 'The Dog Stars' starring Jacob Elordi, flopped. The film, about a pilot and German Shepherd who survive a global pandemic, opened in fifth place with USD 8 million for 20th Century Studios. It added USD 11.3 million overseas, a poor result for a film that cost between USD 70 million and USD 100 million to make.

# Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' overtakes James Cameron's 'Avatar: The Way Of Water' with USD 2.33 billion haul; becomes third highest-grossing film of all time
## 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' hits USD 2.33 billion
For the fifth weekend in a row, 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' topped the North American box office. It grossed USD 22.2 million in U.S. and Canadian theatres, according to studio estimates Sunday, bringing its worldwide total to USD 2.33 billion and making it the third highest-grossing film of all time.
texts.4:
# Tom Holland's 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' overtakes James Cameron's 'Avatar: The Way Of Water' with USD 2.33 billion haul; becomes third highest-grossing film of all time
## 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' beats 'Avatar: The Way of Water'
The Tom Holland-led superhero blockbuster with its earnings crossing the USD 2.33 billion mark, has now edged past 'Avatar: The Way of Water', which finished its theatrical run with approximately USD 2.32 billion. The film's latest earnings represent a drop of just 44% from week 4.

## 'Coyote vs. Acme' off to a flying start
Three years after Warner Bros. abruptly canned 'Coyote vs. Acme,' the Looney Tunes feature film that was given a new lease on life by Ketchup Entertainment debuted with an estimated USD 15.5 million in ticket sales over the weekend.'Coyote vs. Acme', which had been relegated to the dust heap, fared best of the newcomers, debuting in second place. The film, however, scored a decent, hard-earned opening. In 2023, Warner Bros. canceled any release of the completed film, preferring to take a tax write off on a movie originally produced for its streaming service, HBO Max. Warner also shelved 'Batgirl' and 'Scoob! Holiday Haunt', both of which remain unreleased.'Coyote vs. Acme', based on an Ian Frazier 'Shouts and Murmurs' New Yorker column, is about Wile E. Coyote suing the Acme Corporation for its faulty products. It stars Will Forte, John Cena, Lana Condor and Eric Bauza. The film, a hybrid of live-action and animation directed by Dave Green, cost USD 70 million to make. But despite good test screening scores, Warner Bros. opted to ax the completed film. After an outcry, the studio put the film up for sale. Early last year, Ketchup Entertainment acquired worldwide distribution rights for about USD 50 million.Reviews and audience scores were also good. Moviegoers gave it an "A" CinemaScore. Critics were just as enthusiastic. On Rotten Tomatoes, it rated 95% fresh.While the result might have counted as a disappointment for some USD 70 million movies, the opening weekend for 'Coyote vs. Acme' was the best ever for Ketchup. The indie distributor's previous high was 2024's 'The Day the Earth Blew Up' (a $3.1 million opening), another Warner-made Looney Tunes castoff.

_**Avatar**_ is a 2009 epic science fiction film written and directed by James Cameron. It features an ensemble cast including Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Stephen Lang, Michelle Rodriguez, and Sigourney Weaver. It is the first installment in the _Avatar_ film series. It is set in the mid-22nd century, when humans are colonizing Pandora, a lush habitable moon, in order to mine the valuable mineral unobtanium.[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(2009_film)#cite_note-14) The expansion of the mining colony threatens the existence of a local tribe of [Na'vi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fictional_universe_of_Avatar#Na'vi "Fictional universe of Avatar"), a humanoid species indigenous to Pandora. The title of the film refers to an "avatar", which is a genetically engineered Na'vi body remotely operated from the brain of a human, and which is used to interact with the Na'vi.
Development of _Avatar_ began in 1994, when Cameron wrote an 80-page treatment for the film. Filming was due to take place after the completion of Cameron's 1997 film _Titanic_, for a planned release in 1999; however, according to Cameron, the necessary technology was not yet available to achieve his vision of the film. Work on the fictional constructed[language of the Na'vi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Na'vi_language "Na'vi language") began in 2005, and Cameron began developing the screenplay and fictional universe in early 2006.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(2009_film)#cite_note-USCMarshall-15)_Avatar_ was budgeted at $237 million, due to the groundbreaking array of new visual effects Cameron achieved in cooperation with Weta Digital. Some estimates put the cost at between $280 million and $310 million for production, and at $150 million for promotion. The film made extensive use of 3D computer graphics and new motion capture filming techniques, and reunited Cameron with his _Titanic_ co-producer Jon Landau.

_Avatar_ premiered at the Odeon Leicester Square theater in London on December 10, 2009, and was released in the United States on December 18 by 20th Century Fox. The film received positive reviews from critics, who praised its groundbreaking visual effects, though the plot received criticism for being derivative. The film broke several box office records, including becoming the highest-grossing film of all time from 2010 to 2019 and again from 2021 to 2026. It also became the first film to gross more than $2 billion, and was the best-selling video title of 2010 in the United States. Adjusted for inflation, _Avatar_ grossed around $4 billion, making it the second-highest-grossing film behind _Gone with the Wind_ (1939).
_Avatar_ received nine nominations at the 82nd Academy Awards, winning three awards, and received numerous other accolades. Its success led to an increase in popularity of 3D films, and to electronics manufacturers releasing 3D televisions.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(2009_film)#cite_note-16) Two sequels have been released: _Avatar: The Way of Water_ (2022) and _Avatar: Fire and Ash_ (2025), with two more in development.

texts.3:
_**Avatar**_ is a 2009 epic science fiction film written and directed by James Cameron. It features an ensemble cast including Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña, Stephen Lang, Michelle Rodriguez, and Sigourney Weaver. It is the first installment in the _Avatar_ film series. It is set in the mid-22nd century, when humans are colonizing Pandora, a lush habitable moon, in order to mine the valuable mineral unobtanium.[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(2009_film)#cite_note-14) The expansion of the mining colony threatens the existence of a local tribe of [Na'vi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fictional_universe_of_Avatar#Na'vi "Fictional universe of Avatar"), a humanoid species indigenous to Pandora. The title of the film refers to an "avatar", which is a genetically engineered Na'vi body remotely operated from the brain of a human, and which is used to interact with the Na'vi.
Development of _Avatar_ began in 1994, when Cameron wrote an 80-page treatment for the film. Filming was due to take place after the completion of Cameron's 1997 film _Titanic_, for a planned release in 1999; however, according to Cameron, the necessary technology was not yet available to achieve his vision of the film. Work on the fictional constructed[language of the Na'vi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Na'vi_language "Na'vi language") began in 2005, and Cameron began developing the screenplay and fictional universe in early 2006.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(2009_film)#cite_note-USCMarshall-15)_Avatar_ was budgeted at $237 million, due to the groundbreaking array of new visual effects Cameron achieved in cooperation with Weta Digital. Some estimates put the cost at between $280 million and $310 million for production, and at $150 million for promotion. The film made extensive use of 3D computer graphics and new motion capture filming techniques, and reunited Cameron with his _Titanic_ co-producer Jon Landau.
texts.4:
_Avatar_ premiered at the Odeon Leicester Square theater in London on December 10, 2009, and was released in the United States on December 18 by 20th Century Fox. The film received positive reviews from critics, who praised its groundbreaking visual effects, though the plot received criticism for being derivative. The film broke several box office records, including becoming the highest-grossing film of all time from 2010 to 2019 and again from 2021 to 2026. It also became the first film to gross more than $2 billion, and was the best-selling video title of 2010 in the United States. Adjusted for inflation, _Avatar_ grossed around $4 billion, making it the second-highest-grossing film behind _Gone with the Wind_ (1939).
_Avatar_ received nine nominations at the 82nd Academy Awards, winning three awards, and received numerous other accolades. Its success led to an increase in popularity of 3D films, and to electronics manufacturers releasing 3D televisions.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar_(2009_film)#cite_note-16) Two sequels have been released: _Avatar: The Way of Water_ (2022) and _Avatar: Fire and Ash_ (2025), with two more in development.
